verdict.rationale: Restate's own flow-control feature documents concurrency limits applied per scope to protect downstream services and keep scheduling fair. That directly addresses capping concurrency so one hot customer can't starve others. However, the evidence never documents rate limits (requests per time window), and it does not spell out which scopes exist (workflow, key, tenant). missing for 10: documented rate limiting, explicit per-workflow/per-key/per-tenant scope definitions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I cap concurrency and set rate limits per workflow, per key, or per tenant so one hot customer can't starve the rest

citations.quote: Shape traffic with concurrency limits per scope to control cost, protect downstream services, and keep scheduling fair.
Flow control lets you shape the traffic flowing through Restate instead of letting invocations run unbounded.
Shape and limit concurrent invocations with scope
A concurrency limit puts a ceiling on that cost.
